simple: a queue of GPU jobs that are done in the order you put them in.
analogy: one order spike at the pass.
precise: a sequence of operations (copies, kernels, event records, waits) that execute in issue order; operations in different streams may run concurrently. The runtime creates one with cudaStreamCreate or cudaStreamCreateWithFlags. Not a C++ I/O stream (std::ostream) and not the HD Audio stream of DR302.
source: D1 of F6-28: NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide" — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); H1 of F6-28: CUDA 12.0 headers as installed in the build container (Ubuntu package nvidia-cuda-dev 12.0.146~12.0.1-4build4), read in this build: cuda_runtime_api.h (section "API synchronization behavior"
related: Legacy default stream (stream 0, the NULL stream)

term: Legacy default stream (stream 0, the NULL stream)
simple: the queue your work goes to when you name no stream.
analogy: the old spike by the door that makes every other spike wait.
precise: the per-context implicit stream used when no stream argument is given; nvcc's help text describes it as "per context, implicitly synchronizes with other streams", and nvcc uses it by default.
source: R4 of F6-28: lab run in this build (nvcc --help, the --default-stream entry, recorded in this build); D1 of F6-28: NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide" — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a queue that never waits for the old default queue.
analogy: a spike that ignores the old spike by the door.
precise: a stream created with the flag cudaStreamNonBlocking, which the header documents as: work in it "may run concurrently with work in stream 0 (the NULL stream)" and the stream "should perform no implicit synchronization with stream 0".
source: H1 of F6-28: CUDA 12.0 headers as installed in the build container (Ubuntu package nvidia-cuda-dev 12.0.146~12.0.1-4build4), read in this build: cuda_runtime_api.h (section "API synchronization behavior"
related: Legacy default stream (stream 0, the NULL stream)

simple: each CPU thread gets its own ordinary default queue.
analogy: each waiter gets a private spike instead of sharing the old one.
precise: selected with nvcc's --default-stream per-thread; nvcc describes it as "a normal CUDA stream (per thread, does not implicitly synchronize with other streams)". The handle cudaStreamPerThread names it explicitly.
source: R4 of F6-28: lab run in this build (nvcc --help, the --default-stream entry, recorded in this build); H1 of F6-28: CUDA 12.0 headers as installed in the build container (Ubuntu package nvidia-cuda-dev 12.0.146~12.0.1-4build4), read in this build: cuda_runtime_api.h (section "API synchronization behavior"
related: Legacy default stream (stream 0, the NULL stream)

simple: a marker you drop into a queue to know when the queue gets that far.
analogy: the brass token dropped on a spike.
precise: an object that cudaEventRecord fills with "the contents of stream at the time of this call"; cudaEventQuery, cudaEventSynchronize and cudaStreamWaitEvent then examine or wait for completion of that captured work, and two completed events give an elapsed time. Not the same as a probability event (MA202) or a Windows event object (OS304).
source: H1 of F6-28: CUDA 12.0 headers as installed in the build container (Ubuntu package nvidia-cuda-dev 12.0.146~12.0.1-4build4), read in this build: cuda_runtime_api.h (section "API synchronization behavior"
related: Legacy default stream (stream 0, the NULL stream)

simple: a rule that one queue must wait for a point in another queue.
analogy: the note "wait until the token is reached" pinned on spike two.
precise: cudaStreamWaitEvent(stream, event, 0) "makes all future work submitted to stream wait for all work captured in event"; the wait is performed on the device when applicable, so the host does not block.
source: H1 of F6-28: CUDA 12.0 headers as installed in the build container (Ubuntu package nvidia-cuda-dev 12.0.146~12.0.1-4build4), read in this build: cuda_runtime_api.h (section "API synchronization behavior"
related: Legacy default stream (stream 0, the NULL stream)

simple: the call returns before the GPU has done the job.
analogy: Priya pins the slip and walks away; she does not stand and watch it cook.
precise: a call that may return before the operation completes, for example kernel launches and cudaMemcpyAsync in most directions; the header's section "API synchronization behavior" lists the exceptions.
source: H1 of F6-28: CUDA 12.0 headers as installed in the build container (Ubuntu package nvidia-cuda-dev 12.0.146~12.0.1-4build4), read in this build: cuda_runtime_api.h (section "API synchronization behavior"
related: Legacy default stream (stream 0, the NULL stream)

simple: a picture of what each worker did over time.
analogy: a wall chart with one row per station and a bar for every job.
precise: a time axis with one lane per execution resource (copy engine, compute, host thread) and one bar per operation; profilers such as Nsight Systems record them (F6-32), and this chapter's model computes them.
source: Course definition written in F6-28 (no external source cited for this term); pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)
related: Legacy default stream (stream 0, the NULL stream)

simple: ordinary memory from new, malloc or std::vector, which the operating system may move or swap.
analogy: crates in the storeroom, which the storeroom staff rearrange.
precise: host memory whose pages the operating system may relocate or page out (F1-38); for copies from it the CUDA driver first copies the data into "staging memory for DMA transfer".
source: H1 of F6-29: CUDA 12.0 headers as installed (Ubuntu package nvidia-cuda-dev 12.0.146~12.0.1-4build4), read in this build: cuda_runtime_api.h section "API synchronization behavior"

simple: host memory the operating system promises not to move, so the GPU can read it directly.
analogy: crates on the loading dock.
precise: host memory allocated with cudaMallocHost or cudaHostAlloc, or registered with cudaHostRegister, that is "page-locked and accessible to the device" and "can be read or written with much higher bandwidth than pageable memory". Already defined in F1-62; this chapter adds its role in overlap.
source: H1 of F6-29: CUDA 12.0 headers as installed (Ubuntu package nvidia-cuda-dev 12.0.146~12.0.1-4build4), read in this build: cuda_runtime_api.h section "API synchronization behavior"

simple: one piece of a big job, copied and processed on its own.
analogy: one batch of twenty-five crates.
precise: a contiguous slice of the input whose copy in, kernel and copy out form one in-order sequence in one stream, so that different slices can be in different stages at the same time.
source: Course definition written in F6-29 (no external source cited for this term); pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: doing different steps for different pieces at the same time.
analogy: porters carrying batch two in while cooks cook batch one and another porter carries batch zero out.
precise: a schedule in which chunk k+1's copy in, chunk k's kernel and chunk k−1's copy out run concurrently on different engines; with C equal chunks its time is about serial / C + (C − 1) / C × (slowest stage), plus per-chunk costs (this chapter's derivation).
source: Course definition written in F6-29 (no external source cited for this term); pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the order in which the CPU hands the GPU its jobs.
analogy: pinning all of batch one's slips, then batch two's (depth-first), or all "carry in" slips first, then all "cook" slips (breadth-first).
precise: depth-first issues copy in, kernel, copy out per chunk; breadth-first issues all copies in, then all kernels, then all copies out. Results are the same; on hardware whose engines take work in issue order, the timelines can differ (Listing 2's model).
source: Course definition written in F6-29 (no external source cited for this term); pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how close the real pipeline came to the plan.
analogy: the evening's actual finish time against the shift plan.
precise: measured pipeline time divided by predicted time, the quantity milestone E8 bounds ("within 20 %").
source: C1 of F6-29: Systems Curriculum

simple: a recorded plan of GPU work, with arrows that say what must wait for what.
analogy: the laminated menu card with arrows between courses.
precise: an object of type cudaGraph_t made of nodes (kernel launches, copies, memsets, event operations, host functions, child graphs) and dependency edges; it describes work but does not run it.
source: D1 of F6-30: NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide" — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); H1 of F6-30: CUDA 12.0 headers as installed in the build container

simple: a node is one job; an edge is a "wait for" arrow between two jobs.
analogy: one course on the card; an arrow from the sauce to the dessert.
precise: a node is created with a call such as cudaGraphAddKernelNode (with a list of dependencies) or by stream capture; an edge from node A to node B means B may start only after A completes. Not the edges of a road map in MA102, although the mathematics (a directed acyclic graph) is the same.
source: H1 of F6-30: CUDA 12.0 headers as installed in the build container

simple: the ready-to-run version of a graph, checked and prepared once.
analogy: the card after Joseph has laminated it.
precise: a cudaGraphExec_t made by cudaGraphInstantiate, which validates "any structural constraints or intra-node constraints which were not previously validated"; it is launched with cudaGraphLaunch and destroyed with cudaGraphExecDestroy.
source: H1 of F6-30: CUDA 12.0 headers as installed in the build container

simple: recording the jobs you put into a stream instead of running them.
analogy: Joseph copies each slip onto the card instead of sending it to the cooks.
precise: between cudaStreamBeginCapture(s, mode) and cudaStreamEndCapture(s, &graph), "all operations pushed into the stream will not be executed, but will instead be captured into a graph".
source: H1 of F6-30: CUDA 12.0 headers as installed in the build container

simple: one call that starts all the jobs of an executable graph.
analogy: "serve the card".
precise: cudaGraphLaunch(exec, stream) executes the graph in a stream; "each launch is ordered behind both any previous work in stream and any previous launches of graphExec", and only one instance of an executable graph may execute at a time.
source: H1 of F6-30: CUDA 12.0 headers as installed in the build container

simple: the time spent starting a kernel, not running it.
analogy: the time Amara spends writing and carrying a slip.
precise: the host time of a launch call plus any gap on the GPU between the end of one kernel and the start of the next; this course's launch model (Listing 3) treats both as parameters, because no values could be measured in this build (AH-23).
source: Course definition written in F6-30 (no external source cited for this term); pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: changing the values inside a prepared graph without preparing it again.
analogy: updating the card's salt line without writing a new card.
precise: cudaGraphExecKernelNodeSetParams changes one kernel node's parameters for future launches; cudaGraphExecUpdate copies the node parameters of a "topologically identical graph" into the executable graph, or fails with a reason.
source: H1 of F6-30: CUDA 12.0 headers as installed in the build container

simple: memory with one address that both the CPU and the GPU can use; the system moves the data to whoever uses it.
analogy: crates with one number valid in both stores, moved by runners.
precise: memory allocated with cudaMallocManaged or declared __managed__; the header says the pointer "is valid on the CPU and on all GPUs in the system that support managed memory" and "all accesses to this pointer must obey the Unified Memory programming model". It is released with cudaFree.
source: H1 of F6-31: CUDA 12.0 headers as installed in the build container; D1 of F6-31: NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide" — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: moving a page of data to the memory of the processor that uses it.
analogy: a runner carrying a crate from one store to the other.
precise: on systems where devices report concurrentManagedAccess, "managed memory can migrate to any processor's memory at any time", and "the Unified Memory driver will employ heuristics to maintain data locality and prevent excessive page faults".
source: H1 of F6-31: CUDA 12.0 headers as installed in the build container

simple: the moment a processor reaches for data that is not where it can use it, and must wait for it.
analogy: the cook reaches for crate 812, it is not there, and the cook waits for the runner.
precise: an access to a virtual page that has no valid mapping for the accessing processor, resolved by the operating system (CPU, F1-38, F3-21) or by the Unified Memory driver (GPU) before the access is retried.
source: D1 of F6-31: NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide" — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D4 of F6-31: Remzi H. Arpaci-Dusseau and Andrea C. Arpaci-Dusseau, "Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces" — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: moving data to where it will be needed before anyone asks for it.
analogy: telling the runners in advance which crates to bring.
precise: cudaMemPrefetchAsync(ptr, bytes, dstDevice, stream) migrates a managed range to a GPU or, with cudaCpuDeviceId, to host memory, as an operation in a stream; the header calls it "not required for functionality" and says it "only serves to improve performance".
source: H1 of F6-31: CUDA 12.0 headers as installed in the build container

simple: hints that tell the system how you will use a range of memory.
analogy: notes on a crate: "mostly for tasting", "keep in the pantry", "the larder will look at this too".
precise: cudaMemAdvise with cudaMemAdviseSetReadMostly, cudaMemAdviseSetPreferredLocation or cudaMemAdviseSetAccessedBy (and their unset forms), each with documented effects on duplication, migration and mapping.
source: H1 of F6-31: CUDA 12.0 headers as installed in the build container

simple: data moving back and forth between two processors again and again.
analogy: crates carried to the larder after every course and back again.
precise: repeated migration of the same pages because two processors take turns accessing them; the header mentions the driver's "page thrash detection and resolution logic", which may eventually pin a constantly thrashing page to host memory.
source: H1 of F6-31: CUDA 12.0 headers as installed in the build container

simple: a page fault the operating system fixes without reading the disk.
analogy: the crate is in the building; it only needs to be put on the right shelf.
precise: the count Linux reports in ru_minflt of getrusage; Listing 2 uses it to count first-touch faults on the CPU.
source: D5 of F6-31: Linux man-pages project, manual pages getrusage — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R2 of F6-31: lab run in this build (build and run of Listing 2 with the university's flags including AddressSanitizer and ...)

simple: a tool that records what every part of the program did over time and draws it as rows.
analogy: Zainab's wall chart with one row per station.
precise: a profiler that traces host threads, runtime and driver API calls, memory copies and kernel executions (and optionally operating-system and library activity) with timestamps on a common time axis; NVIDIA's tool for this is Nsight Systems. Contrast with a kernel profiler (F6-33), which looks inside one kernel.
source: D1 of F6-32: NVIDIA, "Nsight Systems" — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a trace writes down every event; sampling looks every so often.
analogy: writing down every slip the chef writes, versus glancing at each station every few seconds.
precise: tracing records each instrumented event (an API call, a copy, a kernel) with start and end times; sampling records the state (for example the CPU's program counter) at intervals and estimates where time goes. Timelines of GPU work are traces.
source: D1 of F6-32: NVIDIA, "Nsight Systems" — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D5 of F6-32: Brendan Gregg, "Systems Performance: Enterprise and the Cloud" — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: labels your program puts on the timeline: "from here to here I was doing X", or "X happened now".
analogy: the head chef writing "Friday specials" on her own row of the chart.
precise: calls of the NVIDIA Tools Extension library such as nvtxRangePushA/nvtxRangePop (a nested range on the calling thread) and nvtxMarkA (an instantaneous marker); the installed header says the library "introduces close to zero overhead if no tool is attached".
source: H2 of F6-32: the NVTX version 3 header installed with the toolkit, nvtx3/nvToolsExt.h, read in this ...

simple: one row of the chart, for one thing that can be busy.
analogy: the porters-in row.
precise: a horizontal track for one execution resource or source of events: a host thread, the CUDA API calls of that thread, a stream, a copy direction, kernels on a device. Bars in one lane of an engine do not overlap; overlap appears between lanes (F6-28).
source: Course definition written in F6-32 (no external source cited for this term); pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how much of the time a row is doing something, and the empty stretches in between.
analogy: how much of the evening the cooks were actually cooking.
precise: the sum of bar lengths in a lane divided by the timeline's total time; an idle gap is an interval with no bar in that lane. Listing 3 computes both from an export.
source: Course definition written in F6-32 (no external source cited for this term); pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the time during which a copy and a kernel ran at the same moment.
analogy: the time when porters and cooks were both busy.
precise: the measure of the union of intervals where at least one copy-lane bar and at least one compute-lane bar are active; zero overlap with streams in the code means something serialised them.
source: Course definition written in F6-32 (no external source cited for this term); pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a call where the CPU stops and waits for the GPU.
analogy: the head chef standing at the door until the porter is back.
precise: a runtime call that returns only after GPU work completes, for example cudaStreamSynchronize, cudaEventSynchronize, and copies documented as synchronous, such as any device-to-host copy into pageable memory, which "will return only once the copy has completed".
source: H1 of F6-32: CUDA 12.0 headers as installed in the build container (Ubuntu package nvidia-cuda-dev 12.0.146~12.0.1-4build4), read in this build: cuda_runtime_api.h, the section "API synchronization behavior"

simple: a tool that looks inside one GPU kernel and reports how busy each part of the GPU was while it ran.
analogy: the inspector who studies one station.
precise: a profiler that collects hardware performance counters for individual kernel launches and derives metrics such as achieved memory throughput and compute throughput relative to the device's peak; NVIDIA's tool for this is Nsight Compute. Not the whole-program view of F6-32.
source: D1 of F6-33: NVIDIA, "Nsight Compute" — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a picture that says the fastest a kernel can possibly go, given how much arithmetic it does per byte it moves.
analogy: the inspector's two limits, knives and pantry door.
precise: attainable performance = min(peak FLOP/s, arithmetic intensity × peak memory bandwidth), drawn on log–log axes as a slanted memory roof meeting a flat compute roof. Already defined for CPUs in F2-56.
source: D3 of F6-33: Samuel Williams, Andrew Waterman, David Patterson, "Roofline: An Insightful Visual Performance Model for Multicore Architectures" — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how much calculating a kernel does for each byte it reads or writes.
analogy: chopping per crate.
precise: floating-point operations divided by bytes of memory traffic, in FLOP/byte; the chapter counts DRAM-level traffic as the bytes the kernel's global loads and stores request (a lower bound when caches help, an upper bound when accesses are uncoalesced). Defined for GEMM in F6-21.
source: D3 of F6-33: Samuel Williams, Andrew Waterman, David Patterson, "Roofline: An Insightful Visual Performance Model for Multicore Architectures" — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the intensity at which a kernel stops being limited by memory and starts being limited by arithmetic.
analogy: the recipe at which the knives and the door are equally busy.
precise: peak FLOP/s divided by peak bandwidth, in FLOP/byte.
source: D3 of F6-33: Samuel Williams, Andrew Waterman, David Patterson, "Roofline: An Insightful Visual Performance Model for Multicore Architectures" — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how close a kernel came to the hardware's maximum for one kind of work.
analogy: "the door was in use 85 % of the evening".
precise: a kernel profiler's summary metric of achieved throughput as a percentage of the theoretical peak, reported separately for compute and memory units; the curriculum's topic list names "speed-of-light and memory charts" as what to read. Exact metric names: unverified box in Layer 2.
source: C1 of F6-33: Systems Curriculum (this project), section 13.2 topic "Profiling and the roofline model"; D1 of F6-33: NVIDIA, "Nsight Compute" — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: running the same kernel several times so that a profiler can collect more counters than it can read at once.
analogy: the inspector asking for the same batch of soup three times, counting different things each time.
precise: a kernel profiler technique in which the kernel launch is repeated, with memory saved and restored between passes, to collect metric groups that do not fit in one pass; it makes profiled durations differ from unprofiled ones.
source: D1 of F6-33: NVIDIA, "Nsight Compute" — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a longer piece of code that runs only for rare, difficult inputs.
analogy: the special procedure for a frozen crate.
precise: in the SASS of an IEEE-rounded single-precision division in this build, a check instruction (FCHK) decides whether the fast reciprocal-based result can be used; otherwise the code calls a subroutine (CALL.REL.NOINC) (R5).
source: Course definition written in F6-33 (no external source cited for this term); pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: NVIDIA's portable GPU assembly language, one level below CUDA C++.
analogy: the recipe in the guild's general recipe language.
precise: a virtual instruction set with unlimited typed virtual registers (%r, %rd, %f, %p) and explicit state spaces (.param, .global, .shared, .local), specified by the "PTX ISA" document; nvcc emits it with -ptx.
source: D1 of F6-34: NVIDIA, "Parallel Thread Execution ISA" — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R1 of F6-34: lab run in this build (nvcc -arch=sm_80 -ptx kernels.cu, bodies of the two axpy kernels)

simple: the real machine code one GPU generation executes.
analogy: the steward's card for this hall.
precise: the native instruction set of an sm_XY architecture, produced from PTX by ptxas and shown by cuobjdump -sass or nvdisasm; its instructions use physical registers (R0…, predicates P0…, uniform registers UR…) and differ between architectures.
source: D2 of F6-34: NVIDIA, "CUDA Binary Utilities" — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R2 of F6-34: lab run in this build (cuobjdump -sass of the two axpy kernels for sm_80)

simple: the PTX level a program targets, and the actual GPU generation its machine code is for.
analogy: the edition of the general recipe language, and the hall the steward writes for.
precise: nvcc's help text, recorded in this build, says that --gpu-architecture=sm_50 "is equivalent to" --gpu-architecture=compute_50 --gpu-code=sm_50,compute_50: SASS for the real architecture plus PTX for the virtual one.
source: R8 of F6-34: lab run in this build (nvcc --help, the --gpu-architecture entry, excerpt)

simple: the bundle of GPU code images stored inside your executable.
analogy: a folder holding the general card and the steward's cards for several halls.
precise: the container nvcc embeds in the host executable with SASS (ELF cubin) images and PTX images; cuobjdump --list-elf --list-ptx lists them (R9).
source: D2 of F6-34: NVIDIA, "CUDA Binary Utilities" — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a true/false flag that decides whether an instruction does anything.
analogy: "only the helpers whose bowl is empty do this step".
precise: in PTX, a .pred register set by setp; in SASS, P0–P6 and the constant-true PT, written @P0 or @!P0 before an instruction (R2).
source: D1 of F6-34: NVIDIA, "Parallel Thread Execution ISA" — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a value the compiler had to park in memory because the thread ran out of registers.
analogy: the bowl put down on the far shelf and fetched back later.
precise: a store to and load from per-thread local memory (SASS STL/LDL), reported by ptxas -v as "spill stores" and "spill loads" in bytes; local memory is private in scope but resides in device memory (F1-58).
source: D3 of F6-34: NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide" — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R10 of F6-34: lab run in this build (rowsums.cu built with nvcc -arch=sm_80 -cubin -Xptxas -v)

simple: notes in the binary that say which source line each machine instruction came from.
analogy: the steward writing the head chef's line number next to each of his steps.
precise: nvcc's -lineinfo keeps source-line correlation in the cubin; nvdisasm -g prints it as //## File "...", line N comments (R3), and profilers use it to attribute metrics to source lines.
source: D2 of F6-34: NVIDIA, "CUDA Binary Utilities" — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a helper on the GPU that moves data over the link by itself while the GPU computes.
analogy: the trolley porters, who work while the cooks cook.
precise: a direct-memory-access engine; asyncEngineCount is 1 when the device can copy between host and device while executing a kernel, 2 when it can copy in both directions and execute a kernel at the same time.
source: H1 of F1-62 (CUDA 12.0 header, read in this build)

simple: a pretend GPU that this course invented so that the arithmetic is easy.
analogy: a model kitchen used in cookery class, not a real restaurant.
precise: an invented GPU with round numbers (4 SMs, warps of 32; per SM 16 resident warps, 4 blocks, 16,384 registers, 32 KiB shared memory; model latencies 100 and 4 cycles; 256-bit memory at 8 GT/s; host link 16 GB/s with 10 µs per copy) used only for worked examples and models; none of its numbers describe a real product.
source: defined in F1-55 of this university (invented; not a source about any GPU)

simple: the two levels of NVIDIA GPU code: a portable one and the real machine code.
analogy: the recipe in a general cookbook language, and the version rewritten for one particular kitchen.
precise: PTX is NVIDIA's virtual instruction set, kept in binaries for later compilation; SASS is the machine code of one GPU generation (sm_XY), shown by cuobjdump -sass. Example from this build: PTX mov.u32 %r16, WARP_SZ becomes SASS with the constant 0x20 for sm_80.
source: D4 and D5 of F1-57 (PTX ISA; CUDA Binary Utilities) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R3 of F1-57

simple: when a thread runs out of registers, the compiler parks values in memory and fetches them back.
analogy: walking to the pantry shelf to park pieces that do not fit on the tray.
precise: per-thread local memory is private in scope but stored in device memory and cached; ptxas reports spill stores and loads in bytes; SASS uses STL/LDL. In this build, a register cap of 16 turned 0 spill bytes into 416 bytes of stores and 572 of loads.
source: D3 of F1-58 (NVIDIA "CUDA C++ Programming Guide") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R5 of F1-58 (ptxas reports)

simple: limited by moving data, or limited by calculating.
analogy: the salad (door-limited) and the stew (stove-limited).
precise: a kernel is memory-bound if intensity × bandwidth is below peak FLOP/s, compute-bound otherwise; the label describes the roof above it, not how close it runs to that roof.
source: D1 of F2-56 (Samuel Williams, Andrew Waterman, David Patterson, "Roofline: An Insightful Visual Performance Model for Multicore Architectures", Communications of the ACM (curriculum item 75; tier 1): the model, ridge point, ceilings, operational intensity) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)
